create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

metadata.source: OIDC authorization endpoint documented generically; included as shared infrastructure per instructions, though not specific to SAML app acting as IdP.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts when the email matches.
saml.note: Same-email merges across enterprise SSO and existing accounts are documented behavior, not an identity-collision bug by themselves.
Case-variant usernames should normally remain distinct unless deployment configuration changes this behavior.

saml.description: API resource scopes and organization scopes not enabled for a third-party application are ignored in authorization requests rather than causing an error.
saml.note: Missing requested scopes in the granted token can be expected behavior when the app was not configured to request them.

saml.description: Requesting a non-enabled user profile scope for a third-party application results in an error.
saml.note: Authorization failure in this case is expected and should not be interpreted as a broken flow.

saml.description: Refresh tokens issued without offline_access are bound to the user session and expire when the 14-day session expires, regardless of configured refresh token TTL.
saml.note: Apparent early refresh-token expiry can be by design due to session binding.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is requested, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Token format differences are expected and affect how verification must be performed.

saml.description: After signing key rotation, previous keys remain valid for existing tokens until removed.
saml.note: Acceptance of tokens signed by a previous key immediately after rotation is documented behavior.

saml.constraint: Logto acts as a SAML Identity Provider for SAML apps, not as a SAML Service Provider consuming upstream SAML assertions. For protocol=saml, do NOT attempt SP-side saml_login, SAML ACS callback, SAML IdP creation, or SAML assertion forgery tests from the attack catalog; those operations are not documented for this platform in the provided docs.

SAML support in the provided docs is outbound only: Logto issues SAML assertions to your application in SP-initiated flow. Security testing for this profile must focus on application creation/configuration and downstream OIDC/session behavior, not upstream SAML assertion validation invariants like saml_cert_substitution or saml_wrong_audience against Logto.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, update the target application to enable the 'Allow token exchange' setting; otherwise failures are expected and are not security findings.

For I5 token-exchange audience/resource tests, include a CONTROL exchange using a valid subject_token and intended resource/scope. Token exchange responses depend on application enablement and requested resource configuration; without a control, rejection may reflect setup failure rather than audience enforcement.

Refresh token rotation semantics are conditional. When rotate_refresh_token is enabled, public clients (SPA/native) always receive a new refresh token on refresh; other clients rotate when the token is older than one year or >=70% of original TTL has passed. Do not treat refresh-token reuse/rotation differences across client types as I2 bugs.

Numeric sentinel/semantic rule for refresh_token_ttl_days: this setting is unavailable for SPA clients, and even when configured for other clients it is capped by session binding if offline_access is omitted. A refresh token issued without offline_access is bound to a fixed 14-day user session and becomes invalid when that session expires regardless of the configured refresh token TTL. Never assume the configured TTL alone controls lifetime.

For I2 freshness tests involving refresh tokens, include offline_access in the authorization request if you need the configured refresh token TTL to take full effect. Without offline_access, the refresh token is session-bound and expires with the 14-day session, which can mask or confound TTL-based conclusions.

Redirect URI matching for applications supports wildcard patterns only in hostname and pathname, only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For I3/OIDC flow tests, do not assume exact-match-only redirect URI behavior on these app types.

Because wildcard redirect URIs are supported for some application types, tests that rely on redirect_uri rejection must use a value outside the documented wildcard pattern. A URI that matches a configured wildcard is valid by design and must not be flagged.

Usernames in Logto are case-sensitive by default, controlled by the CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME environment variable. For I4 case-confusion tests, 'Admin' and 'admin' should be treated as distinct identities unless the deployment explicitly changed this setting.

Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving enterprise SSO or cross-protocol identity merge, same-email account linking is documented by design and must not be reported as an identity-collision bug unless it violates explicit upstream intent or policy.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into primaryEmail, and only verified phone numbers are synced into primaryPhone. I4 tests that expect unverified upstream identifiers to bind local primary identifiers will produce false positives.

For I4 multi-identity tests on third-party app permissions, requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen. Distinguish 'request rejected' from 'scope silently not granted' according to scope type.

Organization scopes are ignored unless the authorization request also includes urn:logto:scope:organizations. For I5 organization-permission tests, always request urn:logto:scope:organizations together with organization scopes; otherwise missing organization permissions are expected by design.

On the consent screen for third-party apps, only scopes already assigned to the user through roles are displayed and grantable. If a third-party app requests scopes the user does not have, they are excluded. For I5 escalation tests, absence of extra scopes in the resulting token is expected and should be checked against user role assignment.

Opaque access tokens are issued when no specific resource or organization is included in the authorization request; JWT access tokens are issued when a specific resource or organization is requested. Verification strategy must account for token format: use /oidc/me or introspection for opaque tokens, and do not assume every access token is a JWT.

Opaque tokens cannot be used as organization tokens. For I5 organization-bound tests, request organization context and expect JWT-format organization tokens; using an opaque token for organization authorization is invalid test setup.

OIDC direct API calls use application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Token, revocation, and introspection requests must be sent as form-encoded bodies; JSON bodies are incorrect setup and resulting failures are not security findings.

SAML in Logto documentation is Logto acting as the Identity Provider for a SAML Service Provider, not Logto consuming upstream SAML assertions. Do NOT attempt to test upstream SAML ACS-style broker behaviors such as saml_login, SAML assertion signature validation, issuer validation, audience restriction validation, OneTimeUse replay, or assertion ID replay against Logto from this documentation set; those attack patterns target a SAML Service Provider / broker role that is not documented here.

For SAML protocol runs on Logto, the usable runtime flow is still OIDC for obtaining API credentials. The fuzzer MUST use /oidc/token for token issuance and /oidc/me for identity verification after any browser-based authentication flow; there is no documented SAML ACS login endpoint in the provided docs.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled in application settings, otherwise failures are expected and are not security findings.

Refresh token TTL has a documented sentinel-like cap from session binding: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session and becomes invalid after the fixed 14-day session TTL regardless of the configured refresh token TTL. Do NOT assume the configured refresh_token_ttl_days alone controls lifetime; include offline_access when testing long-lived refresh-token behavior.

Rotate refresh token defaults to true. For public clients (SPA/native), when enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh. I2 replay/freshness tests involving refresh tokens MUST account for rotation semantics and use the newest refresh token after each refresh, otherwise failures may be caused by expected rotation rather than a vulnerability.

Wildcard matching is documented for redirect URIs only, not for identity or authorization constraint parameters. Do NOT infer wildcard support for scopes, user identifiers, issuer values, or other auth-binding fields from redirect URI behavior.

Third-party application permission handling is by-design restrictive: requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an error, while API resource scopes and organization scopes that are not enabled for the third-party app are ignored and not shown on the consent screen. I5 tests must distinguish 'request rejected' from 'scope silently omitted by policy' and must pre-enable the scopes being tested on the application.

Organization permissions are ignored unless the authorization request also includes urn:logto:scope:organizations. For I5 organization-scope tests, the fuzzer MUST request urn:logto:scope:organizations together with organization scopes, otherwise missing organization permissions are expected behavior.

Consent-screen grants for third-party apps are limited to scopes already assigned to the user through roles. If a third-party app requests scopes the user does not have, those scopes are excluded. I5 escalation tests MUST provision the baseline user roles explicitly; otherwise missing scopes are due to RBAC filtering, not token-exchange or consent bugs.

For token exchange and impersonation-style flows, the exchanged access token is resource-bound via the resource parameter. I5 audience/resource-binding tests MUST set distinct resource values and verify the resulting token audience/resource context, otherwise a missing resource parameter may produce a general-purpose token shape that confounds the result.

Logto documents that built-in token claims cannot be overridden by custom token claims; conflicting custom claims are ignored. Do NOT treat inability to overwrite standard claims such as sub, iss, aud, exp, or built-in role/organization claims as a bug.

Custom JWT claim scripts can deny token issuance via api.denyAccess(). If token issuance fails in tests on tenants with custom JWT scripts enabled, include a control flow or disable custom scripts; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may be caused by tenant business logic rather than protocol validation.

Logto supports signing key rotation where previous keys remain valid for existing tokens. After rotation, old tokens may continue to validate until the previous key is removed. I3 key-rotation tests MUST distinguish 'newly issued tokens use new key' from 'previously issued tokens remain valid by design'; immediate invalidation of all old tokens is not expected.

SAML app support in Logto documentation is Logto-as-IdP for downstream service providers, not Logto-as-SP consuming upstream SAML assertions. Do NOT attempt to use a SAML ACS callback or forged SAMLResponse against Logto for this protocol run; the documented SAML surface is application configuration, not inbound SAML login.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, enterprise SSO account linking is email-based by design: adding SSO identities links to existing accounts if the email matches. Do NOT flag same-email account merging between enterprise SSO and an existing user as an I4 collision unless the emails differ.

Logto currently supports SP-initiated SAML flow for SAML applications and states IdP-initiated flow is future work. Any test expecting IdP-initiated SAML app behavior against Logto-as-IdP will produce false positives.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, or failures are expected configuration errors rather than security behavior.

Refresh token rotation semantics are conditional: for public clients a new refresh token is always issued when rotation is enabled; for other clients rotation occurs after one year, near expiry (>=70% TTL elapsed), or other documented conditions. Do NOT treat refresh-token reuse or non-rotation outside these conditions as a security bug without controlling client type and app settings.

Refresh token TTL has a session-binding caveat: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. For lifetime/freshness tests, include offline_access if you need the configured refresh-token TTL to take full effect.

Redirect URI matching supports wildcard patterns only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and only in hostname/pathname. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For flow-coherence tests, do NOT assume exact-match-only redirect URI behavior if the app type permits wildcards.

Username matching semantics are deployment-configurable via CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME, default true. For I4 case-confusion tests using usernames, control this setting first; 'Admin' vs 'admin' may be distinct by design.

Logto issues opaque access tokens when no specific resource or organization is requested. SESSION_INSPECT should use /oidc/me for opaque tokens and token introspection when needed; do not assume all access tokens are JWTs in SAML-adjacent OIDC flows.

For I5 scope/consent tests on third-party applications, non-enabled user profile scopes cause an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen. The fuzzer MUST distinguish 'request rejected' from 'scope silently not granted' based on scope type.

Organization scopes are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. For organization authorization-binding tests, always include the organizations scope or the organization-specific permissions will be absent by design.

Only scopes already assigned to the user through roles are displayed and grantable on the consent screen for third-party apps. For I5 escalation tests, ensure the baseline user actually has the requested scopes; otherwise missing scopes are expected and not evidence of over-grant.

Custom token claims cannot override built-in claims; conflicting custom claims are ignored. Do NOT interpret failure to replace built-in claims such as sub, iss, aud, or standard identity claims as a security mitigation bypass or inconsistency.

Password login via direct token endpoint is not generally supported by the main sign-in experience; Logto explicitly deprecates ROPC-style in-app credential collection. If login_with_password is unavailable for a given app, use interactive OIDC flow instead of treating absence as a bug.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications. SAML apps: /api/saml-applications.
